messages.subject: About plotting errors
parts:
Hi ggplot users,

I'm trying to overlay two lines on one graph, but have some problems. 
df1
year  month  day  flow       time
2001    1         1     0.2   2001-01-01
2001    2         1     0.3   2001-02-01

df2
year   month  day  flow       time
2001    1          1     0.3   2001-01-01
2001    2          1     0.4   2001-02-01

I did it like this:
fig = ggplot()+ geom_line(subset(df1, year %in% c(2001:2005)),        aes(x=time, y=flow, color='df1)+ geom_line(subset(df2, year %in%    c(2001:2005)), aes(x=time, y=flow, color='df2')+
 scale_color_manual('', limits=c('df1', 'df2'), values=c('red', 'blue'))
print(fig)

But then it has this error and I don't know where to find out the problem:
Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class uneval

Thanks for your help.

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: About plotting errors
parts:
I think a more natural way of doing this would be to make one dataset and map color based on the origin.

library(ggplot2)

df1 <- read.table(text = "year  month  day  flow       time
2001    1         1     0.2   2001-01-01

2001    2         1     0.3   2001-02-01", header = TRUE)
df1$time <- as.Date(df1$time, format = "%Y-%m-%d")

df2 <- read.table(text = "year   month  day  flow       time
2001    1          1     0.3   2001-01-01

2001    2          1     0.4   2001-02-01", header = TRUE)
df2$time <- as.Date(df2$time, format = "%Y-%m-%d")

df1$origin <- "df1"
df2$origin <- "df2"

xy <- rbind(df1, df2)

ggplot(xy, aes(x = time, y = flow, color = origin)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line()

​If you are hell bent ​on your way, you will have to provide a `data` argument explicitly. There are other things wrong with your example. For instance, a missing quote and geom_line nested within another geom_line.

ggplot() + 
  geom_line(data = subset(df1, year %in% c(2001:2005)), aes(x=time, y=flow), color = "blue")+
  geom_line(data =subset(df2, year %in% c(2001:2005)), aes(x=time, y=flow), color = "red")


​Cheers,
Roman​

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: About plotting errors
parts:
You can have several geoms in one ggplot() call, but they should not be nested within each other. Given your code, you have the 4th and 5th line nested under geom_line().

ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    subset(df1, year %in% c(2001:2005)), aes(x=time, y=flow, color='df1') +
      geom_line(subset(df2, year %in%    c(2001:2005)), aes(x=time, y=flow, color='df2') + # nested within geom_line
                  scale_color_manual('', limits=c('df1', 'df2'), values=c('red', 'blue')) # nested within geom_line(geom_line(scale_color_manual))


The correct way of "nesting" is the way I showed in two posts back. If you use a (decent enough) IDE, it should set the correct indentation. Lines starting with the same indent are equivalent, but if one is more indented, it is nested within one of the above calls.

Cheers,
Roman
